title: OpenCode HTTP Read-Only Session Status Tool
summary: Implemented and live-verified a read-only MCP tool, forgepilot_get_opencode_http_session_status, that authenticates to the already-running local OpenCode HTTP server and probes /doc plus /session/status without creating sessions, sending prompts, aborting sessions, starting OpenCode, or contacting the ForgePilot runner start endpoint. The live tool returned authenticated=true, docReachable=true, sessionStatusReachable=true, docPathCount=113, sessionStatusHttpStatus=200, and all selected session/completion-relevant endpoints present, including /session, /session/status, /session/{sessionID}/message, /session/{sessionID}/abort, /api/session/{sessionID}/prompt, /api/session/{sessionID}/wait, /event, /file/content, and /project/current.
caveats: The first live verification attempt exposed OPENCODE_HTTP_AUTH_FAILED because systemd EnvironmentFile expansion differed from the operator shell probe; the operator then hardcoded the OpenCode server credentials into the MCP env file and restarted the service.
A follow-up bridge fix normalized credential environment values before constructing the Basic auth header; bridge commit cd8b1cb passed pnpm test and hardcoded packet-id lint.
The tool returns metadata only; it does not yet read session messages, wait for session completion, collect outputs, or map OpenCode sessions to ForgePilot runnerRunId artifacts.
The credentials were not printed or committed by the tool or checkpoint.
boundaries: This checkpoint records a read-only tool implementation and live verification only.
No OpenCode session was created or aborted.
No ForgePilot runner start endpoint was contacted.
No execution approval was created, consumed, or authorized.
No local execution clearance was created.
Completion semantics still require a separate packet before being used as evidence for model-run completion.
